question.problem:
Given the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$, which of the following vectors are orthogonal to $u?$

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
We compute the dot product between $u$ and each of the listed vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot (-3)+4\cdot (-1)+3\cdot (-1) \\  & =2+3-4-3 \\  & =-2.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & ={u}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {w}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {w}_{4} \\  & =1\cdot 5+(-1)\cdot 0+4\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1 \\  & =5-8+3 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot x & ={u}_{1}\cdot {x}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {x}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {x}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {x}_{4} \\  & =1\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2)+4\cdot 3+3\cdot (-5) \\  & =1+2+12-15 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the correct option is $w$ and $x$ only.
